What we keep and who sees it
Share this code so another student can open your public profile.
Your friend code can’t be drawn for this account. Go back to your profile.
Other students see your name, section, year and the interests you choose. Your email stays private. Your friend code holds only your account identifier.
Read once for distances on Map or Events. Kept in memory; map requests go to Mapbox.

Turning on \"Remind me 1 h before\" saves the event\'s title, start time and place on your device only, through Android\'s WorkManager, so it still fires offline or after a reboot. Nothing is sent to Firebase. It needs the notification permission, which you can change in Settings. Turning it off, cancelling your registration, logging out or deleting your account removes it from the device.
“I\'m going” keeps your account identifier and when you registered. The event\'s organizers can see who registered. Cancel registration removes it.
Joining a group stores your account identifier with the event and group. Students who can read the event can see its groups and their members. Leaving removes your membership.
Your group can read your messages and send times. Deleting your account removes the author link; message text and time remain with a deleted-account label.

A group stores its event, creator\'s account identifier, member account identifiers, capacity and creation time. Each member also has a per-event record identifying their group. Students who can read the event can read its groups and membership lists; a member can still read their own group after losing access to a private event, so they can leave. Associations cannot read groups. Matching uses your chosen interests, section and year from public profiles; it does not use attendance history or friends in this build. Leaving removes your identifier from the membership list and removes your per-event membership record; the last member leaving removes the group. Account deletion performs the same membership cleanup. A group that others still use keeps its original creator identifier, like an event, without the deleted public profile or name.

Group chat stores the message text, sender account identifier and server send time. Only current group members with verified student accounts can read and send messages; associations cannot access chats. Messages you open may be cached on this device for offline reading; sending requires a connection. Leaving a group ends your access but keeps its messages. Account deletion removes the sender account link from all your messages, including chats you left, while retaining their text and time with a deleted-account label. Message text is not automatically redacted: avoid including personal information. Already cached copies on other devices may persist until refreshed or cleared.

Firebase Authentication processes your sign-in details and email (EPFL for students; your own address for associations). Association setup stores its name, type, about and optional website, with automatic initials. Your private Firebase profile stores your account identifier, email, name, section, year, the interests you choose (optional), account type and creation date. Other students cannot read that profile or your email in the app. A separate public profile holds only your name, section, year and interests, copied from your private profile when you save it. Any verified EPFL student can read it by your account identifier, so that students can be matched and see who is in their group; nobody can list all public profiles, associations cannot read it, and it is deleted with your account. The PolySocial student project team administers the Firebase project. Friends are not collected by this build. My friend code shows a QR code that holds only your account identifier, drawn on your phone and never uploaded; a student who scans it can open your public profile.
Events and who can see them

Event data includes the title, description, category, venue coordinates, date and time, optional capacity and organizer identifiers. Verified EPFL students can read public events and private events that list them on the access list. A manually verified association can also read its own association events. An event venue is a place chosen for the event, not a history of your movements.

Map distances and the Events distance filter optionally use approximate location for straight-line calculations on your device. Map reads one foreground fix and discards it when you leave the Map or background the app. Events reads a fix when a distance filter needs it; a successful fix stays in memory for that Events screen session, including when you switch tabs. Pending reads are cancelled when the screen pauses. Coordinates are not saved to disk or uploaded to Firebase. Browsing still works if permission is denied. There is no continuous tracking.

Google Firebase processes account, profile, event, group membership and chat message data. Mapbox serves map requests for the area you view and processes the network and SDK metadata needed for its service. Optional Mapbox telemetry and geofencing start disabled. Provider information and telemetry choices remain accessible through the information control on the Map. The distance fix is separate from the map renderer.

When you tap “I\'m going”, the event stores a registration with your account identifier and the time you registered. The event\'s organizers can see which accounts registered and how many. Cancel registration deletes it at any time, even after the event; while you\'re in a group it isn\'t offered yet, since cancelling would also need to leave the group, which isn\'t built. Deleting an event deletes its registrations, and deleting your account deletes all of yours. Once you\'re going, you can turn on \"Remind me 1 h before\": the event\'s title, start time and place are saved on your device only, through Android\'s WorkManager, and never sent to Firebase. It needs the notification permission; denying it, or later allowing it in Settings, is reflected on the toggle. Turning it off, cancelling your registration, logging out or deleting your account removes it from the device. Group chat stores your message text, account identifier and send time. Your group can read the messages, and messages you open can be cached on this device. Attendance-based matching, photo albums and data export are not available yet. The matching switch stays Off and does not change any consent setting.

Firebase keeps previously loaded data in its device cache for offline use. Mapbox may cache map resources. The app remembers whether location permission was requested or denied, without storing coordinates in these preferences. Event search and filter selections can survive screen or process recreation; location coordinates stay in memory only. Verification resend deadlines are stored as timestamps under an account identifier and under a one-way digest of the email address, retained across sign-out; successful verification clears both, and account deletion clears the identifier\'s. Deleting your account also clears the Firebase device cache. A local digest of the association signup email remembers the account type until its private profile is saved; it stores no password or raw email. Before verification, Back or Change address on the email verification screen removes the unfinished sign-up when possible (this is not the Delete account option); the deadline under the address digest outlives that removal, so the resend limit still applies to a new sign-up with the same address. Otherwise, account and event data in Firebase are not automatically deleted by leaving a screen.

Students can delete their account in Privacy & data after confirming their password or Google sign-in. This deletes your private and public profiles, your event registrations, group memberships and their per-event records, and your sign-in. It also removes the sender account link from your retained messages; their text and time stay, labelled as a deleted account. Message text is not automatically redacted. It then clears this device\'s cache and your account\'s resend timing. A deletion marker keeps only your account identifier so no profile can be created again under it. Events you created stay, without your name; they keep only your account identifier as organizer. Association accounts are deleted by the PolySocial project team: contact the team privately. Data export is not available yet. Do not publish your account details in a public GitHub issue.

This is a school project prototype. The team is confirming the responsible contact, its private deletion address, and the countries of processing and transfer safeguards for Firebase and Mapbox. These details are not established yet and will replace this draft section. No specific country or safeguard is claimed here.
